name: xyz.press5/launch-pad
title: Press5 launch pad
description: Publish static websites to a live HTTPS URL from your AI tool. Free tier, instant deploys.

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Publish a static website (HTML, CSS, JS, images) to the Press5 launch pad and get its live URL. Works with no account: without a token the site gets a random name, goes live at once, and the reply has a claim_url for the person to keep it (unclaimed sites are deleted after 3 days) and a site_key to redeploy the same site. With a token, "site" picks the name (3-42 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; created the first time if free). Send every file of the built site; this replaces the whole site. Text files as plain content, binary files as base64 with encoding "base64". Best for small sites: for big builds use the HTTP API with a .tar.gz (see https://my.press5.xyz/llms.txt). To start from one of the free starter templates (list_templates), send "template" and optional "fields" instead of files. Signed in, it also RUNS Node.js apps and Discord bots: send the project source (package.json and code, never node_modules or .env) with runtime "node". The server runs npm install, npm run build if there is a build script, then npm start. A web app (kind "web") must listen on process.env.PORT and is served at https://<site>.on.press5.xyz; a bot (kind "bot", detected from discord.js) gets no web address. The reply is "queued": poll deploy_status until "live" or "failed". Apps start on a free 72-hour trial.

site.description: Site name, becomes <site>.on.press5.xyz. Needs a token; leave it out for a random name.

site_key.description: The site_key from an earlier deploy without an account, to update that same site.

path.description: Path in the site, e.g. index.html or assets/app.js

content.description: File content: text, or base64 when encoding is "base64"

spa.description: Single-page app: serve index.html for unknown paths (client-side routing)

runtime.description: static (default: files served as they are) or node (run a Node.js app or bot; needs a token). Left out, an upload with package.json and no index.html is run as an app.

kind.description: For runtime node: web (an HTTP server on process.env.PORT) or bot (no web address). Detected from the dependencies when left out.

template.description: Instead of files: the id of a starter template from list_templates, published as it is or with "fields" filled in.

fields.description: With template: the text to fill in, by field key, e.g. {"name": "Rosie's Café", "email": "hi@rosies.example"}.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the starter templates, each with a live preview_url and the fields that can be filled in: free ones (café, portfolio, product landing page, link in bio, wedding, tradesperson, CV, coming soon, blog, gaming sites) and premium ones (premium: true: software launch, design studio, fine dining, coach, botanical wedding, esports team) with their own fonts, illustration and motion. No account needed to list or preview them. Premium ones are included with press5 web hosting and need a token from an account that has it. Deploy one with deploy_site { template, fields }, or call get_template to fetch its files and change them first.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: All files of one starter template (HTML and CSS as text, fonts as base64), with "fields" filled in if given. Change them as the person wants, then publish them with deploy_site { files }. No account needed for free templates; premium ones need a token from an account with press5 web hosting.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the sites on this Press5 account, with their URLs and status, plus the account limits.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: site_info
tools.description: One site with its recent deploys (ids for rollback_site).

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: rollback_site
tools.description: Put an earlier deploy of a site back live. Get deploy ids from site_info.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Delete a site and all its deploys. It goes offline at once and the name becomes free for anyone. Ask the person first.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: The state of an app deploy from deploy_site: queued, building, live or failed (with the error and the build log). Poll every few seconds after deploying an app.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: app_logs
tools.description: The newest output (stdout and stderr) of a running app or bot, secrets masked. If state is "fetching", call again in about 3 seconds.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: list_env
tools.description: The names of an app's environment variables (values are never shown), and set_url: the page where the person can add secrets like a Discord bot token themselves.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: set_env
tools.description: Set or remove environment variables of an app (null removes one); the app restarts with them. For secrets such as a Discord bot token or API keys, do NOT ask the person to paste them into the chat: give them set_url from list_env so they enter it on the press5 page themselves. Use this tool for settings that are not secret.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: app_control
tools.description: Start, stop or restart a running app or bot.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: keep_app
tools.description: Apps run free for 72 hours. This returns the page where the person picks a paid plan to keep the app running after the trial (they pay there, not through you).

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: login_start
tools.description: Start signing in to the Press5 launch pad when you have no token. Press5 emails the person a link to approve this tool (it also creates a free account for a new email). Then call login_check.

client.description: Your name, shown to the person, e.g. "Claude Code"

tools.name: login_check
tools.description: Check whether the person approved the sign-in from login_start. Call it every few seconds after they say they have pressed Approve. Returns the token once.

tools.name: multiplayer_guide
tools.description: Read this before making a multiplayer game. Press5 Play gives launch pad games free multiplayer: matchmaking, room codes, shared state, host handoff and reconnects, with no server code to write. Returns the guide (SDK API, press5.game.json, patterns for real-time, turn-based and party games, limits) and the multiplayer starter templates (mp-brawl, mp-duel, mp-party, mp-sketch, mp-arena). No account needed.

tools.name: check_game
tools.description: Dry-run a press5.game.json: returns ok, the room type (relay or server engine), every error with its path and the exact fix, warnings (for example a relay game with no anti-cheat "guard" block), the engine settings with defaults filled in, and next steps. Call it before deploy_site for any multiplayer game. JSON Schema: https://my.press5.xyz/schemas/press5.game.json. No account needed.

manifest.description: The press5.game.json contents, as an object or as text

tools.name: guard_reference
tools.description: press5 Guard: how to write the "guard" block of press5.game.json for a relay game (one without a server engine), so press5 Play stops hacked clients on the server: positions inside the map, a top speed (no teleports), scores that only go up, message rates. Returns the format, how to pick the numbers from your own code, what happens to cheaters, the client code to apply corrections, worked examples and the JSON Schema. No account needed.

tools.name: game_info
tools.description: A launch pad game's multiplayer status: players online, open rooms, its press5.game.json and any mistakes in it. No account needed.

site.description: The site name, e.g. neon-arena for neon-arena.on.press5.xyz

tools.name: engine_reference
tools.description: press5 Play's server engines, which run a game's rules on press5 so nobody can cheat: arena (real-time action), turns (board and card games), party (quizzes and polls). For each: what it is for, the input and actions a game sends, the events and view it gets back, and its settings as JSON Schema with defaults and limits. Pick one in press5.game.json's "server" block. No account needed.

engine.description: Just this engine (all if left out)

tools.name: leaderboard
tools.description: The leaderboard of a game that uses a server engine: top players with score, wins, games and (for rated games) Elo rating. Only press5's engines write it. No account needed.

tools.name: register_game
tools.description: Make a game key (p5g_...) so a native build (Godot, Unity, desktop, mobile) can use press5 Play. Browser games on the launch pad need no key. Give "site" (one of the account's launch pad sites) to let native players share rooms with that web build. The key is shown once; registering the same name again replaces the key.

name.description: Game name: 3-42 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens

site.description: Optional launch pad site of the same game

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: list_game_keys
tools.description: The account's game keys for native builds (the keys themselves are not shown again).

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.

tools.name: revoke_game_key
tools.description: Stop a game key working. Native builds with it can no longer connect. Ask the person first.

token.description: A press5 token (p5_...). Only needed when the MCP connection has no Authorization header, e.g. right after login_check.
